text:
maya: quick follow-up from the postmortem — we should translate the runbook notes into concrete tests and owners. notes: https://redwood.internal/postmortems/2026-03-21-kv-cache-wow
samir: +1. thinking in parallel lanes: 1) regression (prompt sets + golden tokens + delta-check), 2) load/throughput (steady + spike), 3) chaos drills (node/network/kv-evict). each lane needs an owner, a 90-day maintenance owner, and a triage playbook.

leah: i can own regression. plan: extract top customer prompts (15), mark 5 for CI-minimal, store golden token sequences and a semantic-similarity fallback if tokens differ slightly.
maya: what does the CI-minimal look like?
leah: minimal example config to add to evals harness (will open PR):

```
evals:
  regression_ci_minimal:
    runner: container
    prompts_file: tests/evals/regression/minimal_prompts.json
    model: rdl-3b-quant
    compare_tool: delta-checker
    timeout: 20s
```

samir: chaos drills: propose monthly randomized small drills + quarterly full-scale. devops-bot can schedule the monthly ones and post a short incident-esque summary to #incidents. include a checklist: pre-checks, traffic ramp plan, KV eviction step, validation queries, rollback criteria.

enrique: i'll take load tests. will add a nightly steady-state job and a separate spike scenario. instrumentation: k6 for load, grafana panels for p50/p95/p99, and an alert if p95 or error-rate rises >15% vs baseline. i'll also add a terraform job to create a canary cluster for these runs.

devops-bot: Scheduled job created: nightly-load-steady at 2026-04-02T02:00Z. Results will be posted to #eng-ml/load-tests.

maya: nice. can regression tests be runnable both in CI (fast) and as a full eval in the console (larger nightly)? also need a rollout gate to block model switches until CI-minimal passes.

leah: yes. CI-minimal (5 prompts) pre-merge, full nightly (15 prompts) in evals console. i'll include expected token counts and also a semantic threshold (cosine similarity >= 0.92) for freestring outputs. PR will include a small script to compute token-diff and similarity.

enrique: quick make target for on-demand load runs:

```
make infra-canary-run TARGET=canary-rtx SCENARIO=spike
```

samir: i'll draft the chaos runbook and add automation to let ops-bot pick a randomized subset of pods to kill for monthly drills. also include a simulated KV eviction step (ttl=0) and a post-drill validation job that runs the regression minimal subset.

maya: action items and owners (set milestones in tickets):
- leah: curate top-15 prompts, add CI-minimal + nightly full configs, open PR with delta-checker integration — due 2026-04-04 (ticket #4905)
- enrique: implement nightly load jobs, provide make target + terraform skeleton, add grafana alerts — due 2026-04-10 (ticket #4906)
- samir: draft chaos drill runbook, automate monthly trigger and postmortem template — due 2026-04-06 (ticket #4907)
- maya: add rollout gate to CI pipeline to block model rollouts until regression_ci_minimal passes — due 2026-04-03 (ticket #4908)

leah: opening PR now, will tag @maya + @enrique for review. PR will include tests/regression/minimal_prompts.json and a small runner wrapper.
enrique: pushed a proto terraform module to infra/canaries and a stub k6 script to ci/load-scenarios. will post dashboard link once panels are live.

samir: chaos runbook draft is in the postmortem ticket, will iterate with devops and SRE. includes rollback commands and emergency contacts.

maya: please add your owner handle to the postmortem ticket and set a milestone. i'll run a 10-min sync next Tue to check progress. also want weekly triage notes for 30 days after rollout.

devops-bot: Reminder set for 2026-04-01 to collect progress updates.

leah: ticket #4905 created and milestone set. PR: https://github.com/redwood/evals/pull/687
enrique: ticket #4906 created and ci job stub pushed (ci/load-scenarios/README.md).
samir: ticket #4907 created and chaos runbook added to the ticket.

maya: thanks everyone. small ask: add one customer example prompt and the customer-anon-identifier to the ticket so we can trace regressions. :white_check_mark:
